extracted.intended_audience: FOIA requesters to the Administrative Conference of the United States (ACUS), ACUS FOIA officers/agency staff, and submitters of business/confidential information
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules governing how the Administrative Conference of the United States (ACUS) processes FOIA and Privacy Act requests, proactive disclosures, consultations/referrals, timing, fees, business information protections, and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference study and recommendation process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Conference may study the efficiency, adequacy, and fairness of administrative procedure used by administrative agencies, develop proposed recommendations and supporting reports, and the Assembly may approve, amend, remand, or reject recommendations; deliberations of the Assembly are public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects for inquiry are developed by the Chairman, Council, committees, and Assembly; committees with staff/consultants conduct studies; reports/recommendations are considered by the Council and placed on the plenary agenda; recommendations may be made to agencies, the President, Congress, or the Judicial Conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign assistance limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistance to foreign countries is limited to analysis of administrative procedure issues, training of foreign officials, and design or improvement of administrative procedure where Conference expertise is indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such assistance may only be undertaken on a fully reimbursable basis including all direct and indirect administrative costs and requires concurrence of Secretary of State or USAID Administrator as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: administrative program and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: "Administrative program" includes Federal functions involving protection of the public interest and determination of rights/privileges/obligations through rulemaking, adjudication, licensing, or investigation (excluding military or foreign affairs functions). "Administrative procedure" means procedure used in carrying out an administrative program, broadly construed to include aspects of organization, procedure, or management affecting fairness, speed, and relation to judicial review, but excluding scope of agency responsibility or substantive policy committed to agency discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions set the scope of Conference activities and what counts as administrative procedure for study and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chairman authority and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chairman is the chief executive, presides at Council and plenary sessions, may encourage federal agencies to adopt Conference recommendations, make inquiries into matters for potential Conference study, and furnish assistance and advice to agency heads upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inquiries by the Chairman are intended to determine whether problems should be subjects of Conference study (not to review results in particular cases). Chairman may request information from agency heads as permitted by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic records treated as records
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic records are treated as records for purposes of the FOIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FOIA rules in this subpart should be read with the FOIA statute, OMB Uniform FOIA Fee Schedule and Guidelines, and ACUS's FOIA Reference Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withholding standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency will withhold records or information only when it reasonably foresees that disclosure would harm an interest protected by a FOIA exemption or when disclosure is prohibited by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where full disclosure is not possible the agency will consider partial disclosure and take reasonable steps to segregate and release nonexempt information. These policies do not create any right enforceable in court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Chief FOIA Officer and FOIA Public Liaison
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency designates its General Counsel as Chief FOIA Officer with agency-wide responsibility for FOIA compliance and designates a FOIA Public Liaison to assist individuals in locating and obtaining records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact information for these officials is posted on the agency's FOIA web page (https://www.acus.gov/foia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive disclosures requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Records that FOIA requires the agency to make regularly available in electronic format (including records requested three or more times, previously released and likely to be re-requested, or of general interest) may be accessed through the agency website; a subject matter index or comparable tool will be maintained and updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information routinely provided as part of regular agency activity (e.g., press releases or adopted recommendations) may be provided without following the FOIA subpart; requesters may contact FOIA Public Liaison for assistance locating proactively disclosed records.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to make a FOIA request (methods and addressing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests may be made using the ACUS FOIA request form on the website, by mail to the FOIA Public Liaison at the provided address, or by fax; mark mail 'Freedom of Information Act Request' for quickest handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requesting records about another individual, include written authorization from that individual or proof of death to aid processing. A request is considered received when logged in by the FOIA Public Liaison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of records required
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests must describe records in enough detail to enable agency personnel to locate them with a reasonable amount of effort; include date, title, author, recipient, subject matter, and any file designations if known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If request does not reasonably describe records, the agency will inform the requester what additional information is needed or why insufficient and offer telephone discussion; insufficient description may delay response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format preference accommodation
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters may specify preferred form or electronic format for records and the agency will accommodate the request if the record is readily reproducible in that form or format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency honors specified preference of form/format if reasonably reproducible with reasonable efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement to pay fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Making a FOIA request is considered agreement to pay applicable fees up to $50 unless the requester specifically requests a fee waiver; agency ordinarily confirms agreement in acknowledgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters may specify willingness to pay more or less; agreement does not prejudice ability to seek fee waiver or reduction later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency responsibility for responding
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency is responsible for responding to a request in all respects except when referring records to another agency; in determining responsive records, the agency ordinarily includes only records in its possession and control as of the date it begins its search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If another date is used, the agency will inform the requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations and referrals procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: When a request involves records another federal agency is better able to evaluate for exemptions, ACUS will either consult with that agency and respond after consultation or refer responsibility for responding to the agency that originated the record (if subject to FOIA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency that originated a record is ordinarily presumed best able to determine disclosure; consultations/referrals are described in paragraphs (b)-(d) of §304.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of referral to requester
rubrics_metrics.description: When ACUS refers responsibility for responding to another agency it ordinarily will notify the requester and identify the agency and the part of the request referred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice informs the requester where portions of their request have been sent for processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: order of response
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency ordinarily will respond to requests according to their order of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the general first-in-first-out processing principle, subject to tracks and expedited requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-track processing (simple vs complex)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency generally uses two processing tracks—simple and complex—and determines track placement based on factors such as number of records requested, pages involved, and need for consultations or referrals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters placed on complex track will be provided opportunity to narrow or modify the request to move to the simple track; ACUS will contact requesters by the most efficient means (phone, email, or letter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unusual circumstances and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the statutory 20-day processing limit cannot be met because of unusual circumstances (as defined by FOIA), the agency may extend time limits but must notify the requester in writing before expiration of the 20-day period and provide an estimated completion date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the extension is likely to exceed 10 working days, the agency will offer the requester opportunity to modify the request or arrange an alternative processing period and will inform of OGIS mediation services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of multiple related requests
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple requests submitted by one requester or a group acting in concert constitute a single request involving unusual circumstances and involve clearly related matters, the agency may aggregate them; unrelated multiple requests will not be aggregated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregation is intended to prevent circumvention of unusual circumstances rules by splitting requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for expedited processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests/appeals will be expedited when they involve (i) imminent threat to life or physical safety, (ii) urgency to inform the public concerning actual or alleged federal government activity when made by a person primarily engaged in disseminating information, or (iii) other circumstances determined by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request for expedited processing must include a certified statement explaining basis; agency may waive formality of certification; decision on expedited processing will be made within ten calendar days and, if granted, the request will be given priority and processed as soon as practicable; denials will be acted on expeditiously on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency cannot provide requested information within two working days, an acknowledgment letter or email will be sent confirming requester’s agreement to pay fees and providing a tracking number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracking number may be used to check status and estimated completion date via contact with FOIA Public Liaison; agency may seek further information or clarification in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to determine grants/denials
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily the agency will have 20 working days from receipt to determine whether to grant or deny a request and will notify the requester in writing immediately upon making that determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice will inform requester of any fee charged and disclose records promptly upon payment; requester also informed of FOIA Public Liaison availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse determination definition and denial letter contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Adverse determinations include denials to withhold records in whole or in part, that records do not exist or cannot be located, records not readily reproducible in requested form, requested item not a FOIA record, disputed fee determinations, or denial of expedited treatment. Denial letters will include the name/title of person responsible, brief statement of reasons including exemptions applied, estimate of volume withheld (if appropriate), indication on released portions where exemptions applied (if feasible), statement that denial may be appealed under §304.8(a) and description of appeal requirements, and notification of FOIA Public Liaison and OGIS dispute resolution services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate of volume need not be provided if volume is indicated on disclosed records or if providing estimate would harm an interest protected by an exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings on partially released documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Records disclosed in part will be marked or annotated to show amount of information deleted and, if technically feasible, the location of deleted information, unless doing so would harm an interest protected by an exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markings help requesters understand what was withheld and why; exceptions apply when marking would itself cause harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business information disclosure limited and governed by Executive Order 12600
rubrics_metrics.description: Business information obtained by the agency will be disclosed under FOIA only under the business information section and in accordance with Executive Order 12,600.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes a special protective regime for privileged/confidential commercial or financial information (Exemption 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of business information and submitter
rubrics_metrics.description: "Business information" means privileged or confidential commercial or financial information obtained from a submitter that may be protected under Exemption 4. "Submitter" includes any person or entity (corporations, state/local/tribal governments, foreign governments) from whom the agency obtains business information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions determine who gets notice and special treatment under the business information rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of business information by submitters
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters should use good-faith efforts to designate by appropriate markings any portion of submissions they consider protected from disclosure under Exemption 4, at time of submission or within a reasonable time thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designations expire ten years after submission unless submitter requests and justifies a longer designation period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to submitters of FOIA requests for their business information
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency will provide a submitter with prompt written notice of a FOIA request or administrative appeal that seeks its business information wherever required, describing the information requested or including copies of requested records or portions containing the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When many submitters must be notified, notification may be made by posting or publishing the notice where reasonably likely to accomplish it; notice gives submitter opportunity to object under paragraph (f).

rubrics_metrics.name: When notice to submitters is required
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice will be given whenever: (1) the information has been designated in good faith by the submitter as protected under Exemption 4; or (2) the agency has reason to believe the information may be protected under Exemption 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets the trigger conditions for the special submitter notice process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitter opportunity to object and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency will allow a submitter a reasonable time to respond to notice and must specify the time period; to object the submitter must submit a detailed written statement specifying all grounds for withholding and, for Exemption 4, show why information is a trade secret or privileged/confidential commercial or financial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond by the specified time is considered no objection; information provided after the agency's disclosure decision will not be considered; information provided by submitter under this paragraph may itself be subject to disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of intent to disclose business information to submitter
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency decides to disclose business information over a submitter's objection, it will give the submitter written notice including reasons why objections were not sustained, a description of the business information to be disclosed, and a specified disclosure date that is a reasonable time after the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides submitters an opportunity to seek court relief or otherwise respond before disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to submitter notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice requirements do not apply if: (1) the agency determines the information should not be disclosed; (2) the information has been lawfully published or officially made available to the public; (3) disclosure is required by statute or regulation (not FOIA); or (4) the submitter's designation appears obviously frivolous (though agency will give reasonable notice of any final decision to disclose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exceptions narrow circumstances requiring submitter notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of FOIA lawsuit to submitter
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a requester files a lawsuit seeking to compel disclosure of business information, the agency will promptly notify the submitter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt notification allows the submitter to consider intervention or other responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding notice to requesters when submitter notice given
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the agency provides a submitter with notice and opportunity to object (or notifies submitter of intent to disclose), it will also notify the requester(s); likewise, when a submitter files a lawsuit to prevent disclosure, the agency will notify the requester(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This keeps requesters informed of submitter actions that may affect disclosure timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals of adverse determinations: filing and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester dissatisfied with an adverse determination may appeal in writing (email or letter) to the Chairman within 90 calendar days of the agency’s denial; appeal should identify the particular determination and provide reasons and supporting information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For quickest handling of mail, mark the appeal 'Freedom of Information Act Appeal.' The Chairman or designee will act on the appeal except where the request becomes FOIA litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responses to appeals and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision on an appeal will ordinarily be communicated within 20 working days and a decision affirming an adverse determination will contain reasons for affirmance including exemptions applied and will inform the requester of FOIA provisions for court review and availability of OGIS mediation; if reversed or modified the request will be reprocessed consistent with the appeal decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal decisions include statement of reasons and information about dispute resolution; reprocessing follows any reversal.

rubrics_metrics.name: OGIS mediation engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Mediation by the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) is voluntary; if the agency agrees to participate it will actively engage to attempt to resolve the dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OGIS mediation is offered as a non-exclusive alternative to FOIA litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal required before seeking court review
rubrics_metrics.description: As a general rule, a requester must first appeal an adverse determination in a timely fashion under the agency's appeal procedures before seeking court review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves administrative remedies and gives the agency an opportunity to correct errors before litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees: charging and collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency will charge for processing FOIA requests in accordance with §304.9(c) and OMB Guidelines and will ordinarily collect all applicable fees before sending copies of requested records; fees must be paid by check or money order payable to the Treasury of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets the payment mechanics and adherence to OMB fee guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of commercial use requests and agency determination
rubrics_metrics.description: "Commercial use request" means a request by a person who seeks information to further commercial, trade, or profit interests (including litigation). The agency will attempt to determine the use and provide the requester an opportunity to clarify if there is reasonable cause to doubt the stated use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct classification affects fee category (e.g., commercial requesters pay for search, review, and duplication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct costs definition
rubrics_metrics.description: "Direct costs" are expenses the agency actually incurs in searching for and duplicating (and for commercial-use requests, reviewing) records to respond to a FOIA request, including employee salary (basic rate plus 16% benefits) and duplication machinery costs; overhead (space, heating, lighting) are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct costs form the basis for fee calculations; the 16% benefit addition is specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplication definition and format preference
rubrics_metrics.description: "Duplication" means making a copy of a record necessary to respond to a FOIA request (paper, audiovisual, electronic, etc.). The agency will honor a requester’s specified preference of form or format if the record is readily reproducible with reasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters' format preferences should be reasonable and technically feasible; certain formats may incur different costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and qualifications for educational and noncommercial scientific institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Educational institution" includes preschools through graduate institutions and vocational education that operate a program of scholarly research; to qualify a requester must show request is authorized by and made under auspices of the institution and records are sought to further scholarly research (not commercial use). "Noncommercial scientific institution" is an institution not operated on a commercial basis operated solely to conduct scientific research whose results are not intended to promote a particular product or industry; similar qualification requirements apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper qualification affects fee category and potential fee reductions.
